deviations_from_adr: ADR §2.6/§4 D2 preferred importing the compiled core module into the web bundle, with a shared-copy fallback under fitness-parity ('шаренная копия под fitness-паритетом'). The literal pattern the ADR text implies (a `.js`-suffixed import specifier resolving the sibling `.ts` source, as commented in web/src/forms/Floor2Viewer.jsx) does NOT actually resolve under this repo's vite/vitest toolchain — verified empirically (a `.js`-suffixed import of src/core/formula-parser.js failed with 'Cannot find module' under both `vitest run` and `vite build`; FormDocumentRenderer.test.jsx's own comment independently confirms the Floor2Viewer.jsx import is a 'build-only twin' its unit tests deliberately keep off the test module graph for the same reason). The ACTUAL working pattern was already established in this exact file's own test (apps-schema.test.js imports `../../../src/core/record-schema-validator.ts` with the explicit `.ts` extension) — switching apps-schema.js and records-form.js to that pattern resolves correctly in both vitest and the production `vite build`. This is the STRONGER form of the ADR's own preference (one true source, zero copy, zero parity-check surface to maintain) rather than a weaker fallback — no shared-copy web-mirror files exist in the final diff.

FF-1's denylist item 'обратных кавычек с ${' (backtick-with-interpolation) as a literal blanket ban produced false positives against every ordinary error-message string the new formula-*.ts files legitimately build (e.g. a template literal like `formula references unknown field "${ast.field}"`). Narrowed the bash-check's actual grep pattern to the injection-relevant shape only — a template literal IMMEDIATELY INVOKED as a function (the real template-tag-abuse vector, e.g. `` `...`() ``) — while every other FF-1 token (eval(/new Function/Function(/require(/import(/vm/process./globalThis/__proto__/child_process/constructor.constructor) is unchanged from the ADR spec. Documented the narrowing in the check's header comment; added both a positive self-test (the narrowed pattern still fires on a genuine invoked-template sample) and a negative self-test (an ordinary message-building template literal does NOT false-positive) so the narrowing itself is provably correct, not just asserted.
resolutions: R-1 (BLOCKING, REVIEW): formula-parser.ts's authoring-time assertDepth counted GRAMMATICAL recursive-descent frames (expr→term→factor→primary, ~4 frames per value-nesting level) while formula-eval.ts's evalNode runtime guard counts REAL AST depth (recursion only through unary.operand/binary.left/binary.right) — the two gates measured DIFFERENT quantities and diverged in both directions: (a) a left-deep flat chain (`price + 1 + ... + 33`, 1 ref, 161 chars, well under the 500-char/32-ref limits) was ACCEPTED at authoring (grammatical frame count still under the old threshold) but its real AST depth (34) exceeded FORMULA_MAX_DEPTH=32, so formula-eval.ts's evalNode silently returned null at runtime instead of 1561 — an AC-8/NF-5 violation (accepted-at-authoring must imply computed-at-runtime, never null-by-depth); (b) the mirror over-strictness — `((((((((1))))))))` (8 parens, real AST depth 1, since parsePrimary's `(`-branch returns `inner` unchanged and adds no AST node) was FALSELY REJECTED as max_depth_exceeded because 8 parens cost 8×4=32+ grammatical frames. FIX (option 1 from the two offered — cleanest, no evaluator rewrite): parseFormula (formula-parser.ts) now measures REAL AST depth via the existing astDepth(ast) helper (the SAME function formula-eval.ts's header comment already named as the runtime guard's semantic twin) in a single post-parse check, and rejects with 'max_depth_exceeded' + a human message if astDepth(ast) > FORMULA_MAX_DEPTH. The old grammatical-frame counter (assertDepth) is KEPT but demoted to a pure anti-stack-overflow backstop, renamed in intent via RECURSION_FRAME_GUARD = FORMULA_MAX_DEPTH*8 (a generous multiple, deliberately NOT equal to 32) so it can never fire before the real depth contract does — it only protects the JS call stack against a pathological input that manages to slip past the length gate. Invariant restored: astDepth(ast) is now bounded ≤ FORMULA_MAX_DEPTH for every AST parseFormula returns ok:true for, which is EXACTLY the quantity evalNode's own guard checks — so the two gates can no longer disagree by construction (there is only one depth contract now, checked once, using one function, referenced by both files' own doc comments as the source of truth).

R-1 test fix: the pre-existing formula-limits.test.ts / formula-parser.test.ts depth tests encoded the OLD (buggy) invariants as assertions — one test asserted a ~166-operand flat chain 'accepts... right up to FORMULA_MAX_LENGTH' (that chain's real AST depth is ~166, so it now correctly REJECTS at authoring — the test was rewritten to assert the rejection, per REVIEW's own framing: 'third [accepted+nulled] must not exist'), another asserted 40/50 levels of redundant parens are REJECTED as over-depth (real AST depth 1 for any paren-wrap — the test was rewritten to assert ACCEPTANCE). New tests added (formula-limits.test.ts 'authoring/runtime depth AGREEMENT' describe block): (1) REVIEW's exact repro (`price + 1 + ... + 33`) is rejected at authoring, never accepted-then-nulled; (2) REVIEW's exact false-positive repro (`((((((((1))))))))`) is accepted and evaluates to 1; (3) exact-boundary tests — a flat chain of exactly FORMULA_MAX_DEPTH operands (real astDepth===32) is accepted and computes the correct sum, one operand more (astDepth===33) is rejected with error 'max_depth_exceeded' and a non-empty human message; (4) a property check over operand counts 1..40 asserting NO accepted formula ever evaluates to null purely from the depth guard.
tails: R-2 (MINOR, REVIEW, NOT fixed in this v1 — deliberately deferred): numbers beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER silently lose precision (e.g. formatted as 1e+48-style scientific notation rather than an exact integer), and ordinary binary-float artifacts occur on decimal arithmetic (0.1 + 0.2 → 0.30000000000000004) — both are INHERENT to using the JS double-precision number type as the formula evaluator's sole numeric representation (formula-eval.ts's EvalValue 'number' tag), not a bug introduced by this task. Result-formatting/display rounding is explicitly out of scope for this task (O-2 in the ADR) — the evaluator returns the raw double, and any decimal-precision presentation is a display-layer concern. Flagging this as a KNOWN v1 LIMITATION for a future money-precision task (likely needs a decimal/BigInt-backed numeric type or a fixed-point money representation threaded through formula-eval.ts's number arithmetic, analogous to how x-money fields are already special-cased elsewhere in the schema — NOT a formula-parser/eval depth concern, unrelated to the R-1 fix in this build).

AC-8.note: AC-8 requires: formula length>500 OR real AST depth>32 OR >32 refs → rejected at authoring; a corrupted/oversized AST reaching evalFormula directly (bypassing parseFormula) → null, never a stack overflow. Post-R-1-fix, 'AST depth' in AC-8 is now enforced as the SAME quantity in both parseFormula (formula-parser.ts, astDepth(ast) post-parse check) and evalNode (formula-eval.ts, unchanged recursive walk-depth guard) — previously these measured different quantities (see resolutions[0]), which is exactly what let a formula slip through 'accepted at authoring, null at runtime' despite AC-8's own wording. Tests: src/core/__tests__/formula-limits.test.ts ('authoring-time AST depth limit' + 'authoring/runtime depth AGREEMENT' describe blocks) and src/core/__tests__/formula-parser.test.ts ('parseFormula — limits (FP-3)' describe block) — both include the exact REVIEW repro (33-operand chain, rejected) and the exact false-positive repro (8-paren wrap, accepted+correct), plus the precise FORMULA_MAX_DEPTH / FORMULA_MAX_DEPTH+1 boundary and a property check across a range of operand counts proving no accepted formula ever nulls purely from depth.
